known_limits: Single project. What this proves about a second consultant's drawings is limited to what the case vocabulary can express without change.
Scores search_plans and the gate, not the composing model: the model's paraphrase is not reproducible run to run.

Absent-case truth is the text layer of every current page PLUS every stored record's quote. The text layer alone was wrong once: EN-001.00 prints PACKAGED TERMINAL AIR CONDITIONERS in an outlined table.

NINE current pages have no sheet number, not seven as this line read until 2026-09-17: the six DEP cross-connection pages, the shed inspection letter, the as-built survey, and one AR gas-change page. A fact that lives only there cannot be checked by sheet, so no case depends on one. Eight of the nine are documents rather than drawings; the ninth is a reissued roof plan whose title-block call timed out at index time.

known_failures.what: Generic prose that repeats more of the question's words outranks the specific record that answers it. 'AC units' is led by the note 'EACH AC UNIT SHALL HAVE A MINI-CONDENSATE PUMP', which matches both words, while the PTAC schedule matches one. HALF OF IT WAS THE SLOTS, NOT THE RANKING: asked about the AC units, five of the eight records returned were two notes repeated, and the PTAC schedule sat at positions six to eight. A note is now one record across the sheets it is stamped on (dedupe_quotes), and the schedule reaches the lead.
known_failures.why_it_is_not_tuned_away: Ranking is similarity-first by design (#589). Special-casing this question would teach the ranker the suite rather than fix the class.
known_failures.evidence: The note is printed identically on M-100.00 through M-105.00 and is vision-read (the M-sheet notes are outlined). The project team confirmed on 2026-09-17 that 588 Boyland has PTACs only and no split systems: it is engineer boilerplate that was not stripped. After the collapse, 2026-09-17: ac-type's lead is M-100.00, M-101.00 and two M-200.00 schedule cells, so the case is no longer scored as a failure — it is STALE, because the schedule cells that answer it are the three known-stale PTAC elements. Whether it PASSES is not known until the re-index clears them.
known_failures.lead_for_a_principled_fix: What remains is the ranking half: one generic note still outranks one specific record when it repeats more of the question's words. The measurement to make after the re-index is whether ac-type passes on the strength of the schedule alone; if it does not, the remaining work is the same idea as a_mention_outranks_the_measurement — an intent-scoped preference for the record that STATES the answer.

known_failures.what: For an attribute question, records that repeat the subject phrase outrank the record that states its value, and with a limit of 8 the value never comes back. Asked how high the sidewalk shed is, the reader returned SIDEWALK SHED, SIDEWALK SHED PARAPET PANEL LAYOUT, TYPICAL SIDEWALK SHED ELEVATION and a permit note — four mentions, no dimension. 8' HIGH SHED is printed on SSP-003.00, SSP-004.00 and SSP-005.00.
known_failures.why_it_is_not_tuned_away: Coverage counts WORDS, which is the rule that fixed the boilerplate cases and is not being special-cased for this one. Nothing in the ranker knows that a record carries a measurement, and teaching it the word 'height' is the attribute table again in a longer coat.
known_failures.evidence: Measured 2026-09-17 on the post-deletion run. The matcher answered this question by looking for a value NEAR the term (answer_attribute, with a hand-written attribute vocabulary that also forgave the live typo 'hight'). Both halves went; this is the half worth rebuilding.
known_failures.lead_for_a_principled_fix: The records already carry the shape of the answer: a quote with a number and a unit in it is a measurement, and an attribute-intent query wants one. Ranking is (coverage, tier, density, type prior); an intent-scoped preference for a record that STATES a value, applied at the same point as best_per_attribute, would order these correctly without a vocabulary of attribute words. It needs its own cases before it ships — a measurement is not always the answer.
